Did members of your unit, the unit that you belonged to in Srebrenica, on the strength of the United Nations Protection Forces, did they use weapons in any case throughout the duration of your mandate in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: When you are referring to the use of weapons, do you mean actually firing?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, I suppose that weapons are only used for the purposes that they are intended for. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Well, simply bearing weapons will have an effect, so to assume that a weapon is used only for shooting is somewhat premature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you use live ammo when you carried out your duties? Did you have any ammo? What kind of ammo did you have?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: We -- or, rather, I personally carried a weapon, calibre 7.62.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did anybody in the unit, as far as you know, get to open fire while on duty, while performing their tasks?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Well, during a patrol we were shot at on one occasion, and we fired back in various ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please give us some details of that event? Who opened fire and from what side? Was that from the side of the Army of Republika Srpska or from the side of the BiH Army? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, we were clearly shot at by positions outside the enclave, so it must have been from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us something about the killing of an UNPROFOR soldier in the safe zone of Srebrenica during those events, immediately prior to those events, and immediately after those events? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, I can't say anything, other than what may have been set forth in possible documents, because I wasn't present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear that an UNPROFOR member had been killed on duty? Did you hear it either from your superiors or from your peers? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you heard? Can you tell us, according to what you heard, when had that happened and how?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Well, all we heard was that a colleague had been injured, and the exact details were disclosed only later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what things were done subsequently in respect of the killing of that soldier? What details were disclosed only later on?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Well, at first we didn't know who it was, and later on data such as who were they and where did it happen came.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether that case was ever investigated by the Dutch Ministry of Defence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to say anything about that. I can assume that an investigation took place on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us, are you not able to answer this question because of the nature of your former job or because of some other secret involved in that? Is that a confidential matter?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Well, not immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm afraid I did not understand your answer properly. Could you please be more specific and tell us why you can't answer my question?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me about details of which I was not aware at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We can read that in the debriefing, and obviously we're going to clarify the matter with those who were better informed. That's why I will no longer dwell upon that with you and I'll move on to another group of questions. Could you please tell me where you stored the weapons that were seized from the Muslims once Srebrenica was proclaimed a safe area? Was it part of your mandate to safe-guard those weapons and prevent those from whom they had been taken to get hold of them again? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Well, all I can say about that is that I was aware that there was a storage area in the city of Srebrenica where confiscated weapons were supposed to be stored.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the DutchBat secure the depot or was it the BiH Army that secured the depot? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, that was DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you meet anybody in your battalion who was on guard detail at that point? Do you know anything about that? Did anybody you personally know provide guard service there?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No. The OP was responsible for that part of my enclave, and we were hardly there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: OP Bravo Company. Bravo Company was responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the course of your mandate, in the course of your tour of duty, were you ever in the vicinity of that place? Did you ever see the place where the weapons were stored, and can you tell us, if you know, how the place was secured?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, I was never aware of that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. When you first arrived, did your command tell you that weapons were confiscated from the Muslims, that the Muslims kept on insisting that the weapons be returned to them, but that the weapons were safeguarded by the UNPROFOR because it was part of the UNPROFOR mandate? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: At the time, all I was told was that there was such a location, but, again, I don't know where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any idea as to what weapons were stored in that location? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No. If any information was given on that, it was the calibres of the weapons and self-made weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were those weapons stored in the Potocari compound once the Muslims left Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution showed us a clip in which Mr. Karremans, on the 11th, informed General Mladic that he had handed over 300 rifles to Muslims. Were you aware of that or were any of the DutchBat soldiers aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we have a reference to the transcript on that, if he's going to be making specifics references to it? There is a transcript of all of those clips.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Well, you wanted me to be as brief as possible. That's why I've speeded up. I didn't want to show the clip that you showed, yourself. I just wanted to put a question in reference to that clip and that refers to the part of the video-clip where Mr. Karremans invited General Mladic to the Fontana, and General Mladic says, What's up, why did you want to talk to me? And then he told him why he wanted to talk to him. And then he told him that he had handed over the weapons to the Muslims. Do you need any further explanation or do you want me to show that part of the clip, that portion of the clip? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can solve this later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps we can clarify that very shortly. Witness, could you tell us if you know anything about handing over of weapons to the Bosnian Muslim Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I was never informed of such -- of anything of the sort happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Maybe we'll be able to clarify the matter with those who were involved on another occasion. And now I would like to move to a group of questions about the NATO bombing. Do you know that a NATO Air Force opened fire on Srebrenica while you were there? And if that is indeed the case, could you please tell us who the NATO Air Force opened fire on, on what side?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no actual firing. The only thing that happened, a number of flares were fired from the aircraft just to frighten people, to scare them off.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On the eve of that day, on the 11th, were you informed by a commander, as a member of the unit, that there would be a NATO campaign in the part of the territory under your control? And in that sense, were some of the troops withdrawn from the territory, some of your troops?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: We were told that F-16s were expected, and that would have been a reason for us to sleep in the bunker.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Just for the transcript, could you please tell us when you heard that, and what night was it that you spent sleeping in the bunker in July of that year?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: It must have been the very evening when we were told that, and it should have been the night of 10th to the 11th or maybe 11th to the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the basis for your conclusion that it was either/or, one date or the other?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Because it is 15 years back in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We will clarify that with those who can provide us with more information, whose report we're going to read. Tell me, did you personally see NATO aircraft and their actions or did you hear it from somebody?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I did see an aircraft, myself. I can't say with 100 per cent certainty that it -- which side it was on. I suppose it was a NATO plane. And as far as I saw, they only dropped flares.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. How far were you from the place where those flares were dropped?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Do you want me to give an estimate of the height at which the aircraft was?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe you did not understand me. Maybe the interpretation was wrong. I asked you how far you were from the place at which the flares were dropped. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I don't know where the flares fell. I only saw them being fired from the aircraft. It must have been -- well, it can be a difference between half a kilometre to one kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you in Potocari at that time? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And how did the population react to NATO sorties, and what were their expectations in respect of the NATO Air Force sorties?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I don't even remember whether there was a reaction or what the expectations could have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And you, as UNPROFOR members and members of the Dutch Battalion, did you know who the actions were targeted against? Were they targeted against the Serb Army or the Muslim Army?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Well, considering that the enclave was being invaded by the Serbian side, I suppose that they wanted to fire at the Serbian positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you this to find out whether you had been told to possibly expect reactions as a result of the NATO campaign and if you had been told who the target of those actions was. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, I have no problem with questions associated with statements, but there was no question in that statement that I could tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, what is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: Were battalion troops ever told what the target of the aircraft campaign was and if they could possibly expect reactions from that side as a result of the NATO campaign, against them?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, I can't really answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, we shall indeed clarify all that with all those who were privy to that information. I'd like to thank you for your answers so far. I've tried to eliminate some of the questions because of the answers you have provided. And now I would kindly ask the Presiding Judge to admit the reports, 1D71 and 1D -- 1D71 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, do you tender the whole report or the pages you used with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we would like to tender the whole report, because that report will be presented to a number of other witnesses who will be testifying about the contents of the report, but I leave it in your hands. I would like to tender the entire report into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, I would agree with General Tolimir on that. It's a short report, and it will be used throughout, I would believe, with the officers in charge, and so I think it's probably a good idea for you to have that now. It's not one of these massive reports, and it would put everything in context as well. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The entire report will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D20, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, do you tender other documents you have used?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. There's something pending from yesterday. I suppose that I should have tendered the informal statement that I presented to the witness yesterday. My legal assistant will send you a submission on that statement. Our witness that we heard yesterday was protected, so I wouldn't go into many details of the issues with regard to that document and the submissions that my legal assistant is going to send you. I take this opportunity to thank Mr. Groenewegen, everybody who have helped me with the cross-examination today. I apologise to the Prosecution if the time that I've taken with this witness has interfered with their plans. And I would like to thank everybody again, and especially the witness, who has been answering my questions during the cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. Mr. McCloskey, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Groenewegen, you will be pleased to -- Mr. Groenewegen, you will be pleased to hear that this concludes your examination. Thank you very much that you were able to come to the Tribunal again. You are free now to return to your normal activities. Thank you again. And we will adjourn now for the second break and resume at 1.00, if there is another witness available, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, there should be an investigator available. I think they probably sent the other witness home, but I will check. But can we get an estimate of cross-examination for the other witness? He has never been cross-examined before. I don't know if it's something that the general was planning. Because if he's available and the cross-examination is short, perhaps we can finish him, but -- and it would be nice to know, in the future, if we're going to bring him back as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I do intend to put several questions to that witness because of those who were participants in the event that he participated in and that are interpreted in many different ways. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The problem, Mr. Tolimir, is that there was a witness available and who was sent back, as I heard, and we lose court time in that way because the indication was not quite clear. We should use, every day, the full time of hearings for the examination of witnesses. First of all, I would like to thank the witness again, and he is now free to leave the courtroom first, and then we can shortly deal with the question of the next witness. Thank you very much, Mr. Groenewegen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We're mindful of the court time, and we are prepared to examine the investigator who is supposed to testify today. I'm sure that he will be talking about the matter that we have already prepared to cross-examine other investigators on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I am told Mr. Janc is available. He'll speak briefly about a preparation of maps that we have for the Court and be available, of course, for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn now and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Please, could you stand. Please read aloud the affirmation on the card which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And now please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think Mr. McCloskey has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you first tell us your name, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: My name is Dusan Janc.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is your current position?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I am an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what team are you assigned to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I'm assigned to the Srebrenica investigation team or the Tolimir trial team.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how long have you been an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I've been here now for four years, so from 1st of June, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you been on that same Srebrenica team from the beginning?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And prior to coming here, what was your position?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I was the criminal investigator with Slovenian police. I worked there since 1993, when I joined the police after I completed my secondary school, so and then I have a different position within the Slovenian police organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So where were you born?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I was born in Kranj, in Slovenia, in 1975.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when did you first go to the police -- start receiving police education or training?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I started my secondary school -- police school in 1989, and after four years I completed it. And I joined the police forces in July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you ever -- were you ever transferred outside of Slovenia during this period of 1991 through 1996?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No, I was all the time in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you ever in the armed forces of any army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No, because when you are a police officer in Slovenia, you don't need to go to the armed forces. So if you serve for police, you don't need to join the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And thank you for being available at short notice to talk about this one exhibit today. And it is Exhibit 06196, and I see that you have it in front of you. You also have a piece of paper that's in front of you. That should be two pages. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, this is my information report I prepared for this testimony, so it relates to this map book. So -- and it has an ERN 0674882-328824 [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I know it has some detailed information in it. So if you do need to refer to it, I don't think that would be a problem. Just let us know that you are referring to it. Now, really, we have called you just to talk about and lay a foundation for the admission of this map book, and we have hard copies that we've provided the Court Officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, while I'm sure it's on e-court, you may want to just have it. It's meant to be something you have with you on your desk, if you so choose, though it will also come up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, first of all, can you tell us who prepared this book?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, do you have the hard copy of this book?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I do, I do have a hard copy, and I've examined it thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we have provided, where necessary, the B/C/S translations for the book for the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just briefly tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a map book which was prepared for this Tolimir trial by Tolimir trial team, and consisting of investigators and the lawyers, and also mainly by the GIS unit of the OTP. "GIS" means "Geographical Information System Unit," so there is a lady who helped us with the creation of this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what's her name from the GIS unit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Her name is Alina Stretton.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just briefly, what is this GIS unit? What do they do?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Actually, they are dealing with the maps. As I explained, "GIS," it means "Geographical Information System." It is a software where you create maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And it's my plan just to briefly go through the book and ask you about where each of the maps came from. I don't want at this time to go into any substance of the meaning or why particular things were done at this point. It's just to form a foundation for the introduction into evidence. But, of course, if there are -- Your Honour, if you do have questions about what you see, of course, Mr. Janc is ready to do that. So let's open it up to the first page, which ends in ERN -- it's actually not the first page. It ends in ERN 3272. It's just the table of contents page. And this, I take it, is just the brief description of each item in the book.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, this is a brief description of each item, each page in this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the first map, then, page 1. No, that's not it. It would be ERN 0701-3273. There you go. Now, this map, we obviously can't read much -- or I can't read very well any of the words on it. Just tell us what this map is. Where did we get it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This map was obtained from the publicly-available source in 1994, from the times, and it is a map showing the area of the former Yugoslavia with all the republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And this coloured section in the left corner, is that meant to be any part of this case or information at all?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No, we are not interested in this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we -- in fact, you can't really read it, in any event. All right. So this gives us a basic background of the borders. Let's go to page 2, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First a question from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. Just for my education, actually --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes. Just for my education, if you could just read out -- as Mr. McCloskey has said, I can't read all the names of the republics in the former Yugoslavia. Can you just read them out for me, please, pointing from this map? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And go back, please, to page 1, to the previous map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can. The first one, I will start from the left to the right, is Slovenia, then it's Croatia, then we have Bosnia and Herzegovina, then we have further Republic of Yugoslavia, then we have Montenegro, and bottom right it's Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you also just give us the border countries that we see, starting with Austria?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yeah, the border countries --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's start with Italy, I think, left to right.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yeah. Indeed, first one would be Italy from the left. Then we go top right corner is Austria, then it's Hungary, then it's Romania. Below Romania is Bulgaria. Then we have Greece and Albania. So these are the surrounding countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, another intervention? Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we please have it explained to us? Here it says that in the left bottom corner, where we see the smaller map with some legends, that that cannot be easily read. However, it is possible to read it, and it contains information about the map which only suits those who wanted to present it in that way, whereas it doesn't say why the national structure or the ethnic structure is presented the way it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I am not interested -- I can't tell what this map says. I don't even know what it has to do with. But it's not something we're asking the Court to review. The ethnic compounds of the various municipalities and areas in Bosnia may be something very hotly interested by the general. It's not something I'm interested in at this point, nor do these maps -- are they designed to display this in any way. So we can -- I'm not asking the Court to review this. If it's something that the general contests with "The Times of London," I can -- just, I don't know what else to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's not necessary to deal with that. Just carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is being proposed here to tender these maps, and yet the Prosecutor says that it doesn't mean anything to him. Then I would appreciate it if we could remove the smaller map from the bigger map, because on the larger map you can see what is being put here, because I feel it is not necessary to show this smaller -- or to admit this smaller map into evidence because it presents details that are only understandable to us who are from that area. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There's no decision of the Chamber yet about admission of this map. We can deal with that later. I think in the moment -- you can deal with that in cross-examination, but now please carry on, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: First of all, tell us who created this map.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This map was created by the Geographical Information System unit of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It is a map of Bosnia and Herzegovina with the entities. So this map was created by the OTP, and it was based on the GIS information we received in 2002 from the GIS data company from Zagreb. So the boundaries you can see inside here, I mean the municipality boundaries and the Dayton line boundaries and the country boundaries, were included into their data and then geographically referenced into the map. Then you have another line which you can see it's approximate VRS/HVO/ABiH confrontation line, and this was taken from the other source, which was HQ Brit for current situation map. So these are details which you can see on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is this meant to be absolute, these lines, or is this meant to give us a general indication of these various lines at various times, as indicated?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No, all these various lines on this map and on following maps would be rough, rough lines, so it's not meant to be in the exact lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next map, which is on page 3. We can again see Bosnia and Herzegovina, and what are -- where did the information come from that we see on this map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Again, for the country boundaries and the municipality boundaries, the information was the same as for the map before. But for -- then we can see the bold black lines. These are the corps boundaries which were taken from Rick Butler's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The corps of what army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, corps of the VRS, VRS Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And just to remind us, who is Rick Butler?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Rick Butler is a military analyst who will also testify in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to page 4. And what is this a blow-up of?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This is the Drina Corps area of responsibility map, where you can see the brigade boundaries inside the Drina Corps area of responsibility. And this one was taken from the map we have obtained from the Drina Corps collection, so with ERN number 00 -- sorry, 0444, and I will read it from my report, 3019.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, the Drina Corps collection, can you just -- there will be a witness about that, but can you briefly explain to this Trial Chamber what that means, what the Drina Corps collection is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: The Drina Corps collection is a huge collection which we received, obtained, I think, in 2004 from Bosnia or Banja Luka, or Serbia. I'm not sure about it. It will be my colleague investigator, Tomasz Blaszczyk, who will testify about it. So we received a huge collection of Drina Corps documents, different documents. Also, maps were included in this collection, and they were stamped here, and this is part of -- this map is part of this collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Just very simply, and I know your colleague will talk about this, but this Drina Corps collection, was that thought to be an archives by the investigative team of the Drina Corps material from the war?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yeah, indeed, that was an archive of the Drina Corps material, documents, from 2009, up to the end of the war in 2005. Also, we have documents from 2006, and it's in total, I think, 200.000 pages, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And we can see that these are the various brigades outlined in that original map from the Drina Corps archives?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just a curious thing. I noticed, right before you were testifying, we see -- can we blow that up a little bit? One more time, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which part of the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Kladanj. That's perfect, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, we can tell, from the legend of the map -- and again I don't want to analyse all this material at this point, but I just -- there's one odd thing I wanted to ask you about. We can tell, from the legend of the map, that this black line that we see between Kladanj and Vlasenica is the approximate confrontation line in April of 1995, and it shows that the yellow part of the Drina Corps would incorporate Kladanj. And I don't think I'm aware of any information where the Drina Corps ever held Kladanj. Do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No, I do apologise, I don't have any explanation why that Kladanj is on that side. I would rather check the original map again to be clear about it. So I would rather check it again. So I have no explanation. But, you know, according to our military analyst, this is the map which was used for this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We will endeavour to bring in that map so you can get an idea of what it is he's talking about anyway, so you can see what kind of maps these things are based on. Okay. All right, let's go to the next page, page 5. And if you could blow that up just to -- so we can read some of the cities, probably getting Srebrenica into the mix. That's perfect. Yeah, keep going. Just get Srebrenica. There, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is this map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This map is a simplified map of the area of the eastern part of Bosnia, which was created by the Dutch Topographical Institute for our purposes. I think we obtained it in -- by the end of 1999, beginning of 2000. And they based their maps on the maps obtained from the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is this map, while it's a simplified map, is it to scale?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I don't think so it's in -- or it should be -- I can -- I don't know. I didn't check that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: So what was with this map was just -- what we received was the empty map, so means that red dots you can see on this map, also on the arrows you can see in this map, and the rectangles you can see in this map, were inserted by us, by the OTP, later on. And the base for these arrows and these dots was the map also obtained from the -- not Drina Corps collection, but from the Zvornik Brigade collection, or it was obtained during the search of the Zvornik Brigade. And the ERN of that map would be 0082-7577. So and these markings were put by military analysts into this map, and these maps were already used in the other Srebrenica-related trials; Krstic trial, Blagojevic trial, and Popovic trial. So and the following two maps are just, you know, blow-ups this same map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And, Your Honours, we will have copies of those VRS maps in their reproduced normal size if you would like to have them for your review as well. And I will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Page 6, you've already referenced that this was just a blow-up of the other map, and all these -- the red lines and the other lines is material that the investigators and the lawyers put on for the case, I take it.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And you see the area of the enclave, Srebrenica enclave here. This was -- this was done by the Dutch Institute. So we haven't inserted this part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One question by Judge Nyambe, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: For the witness, just a clarification. At page 70, lines 17 and 18, you say this map and the rectangles you can see in this map were "inserted by us." Can you indicate the rectangles on your map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The previous map, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: The map, page 5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will be in the map, the third map; not this one, but the one -- the two after this one, where you will have the rectangles. So on this one, you can see the rectangles -- you can see just the red dots, but the rectangles will be on the third map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Just to help us not get confused, when you say "the next map," or "the previous map," it might be good to say, The map on such and such page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do apologise. So it is -- the rectangles will be on the map with ERN 0701-3279.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that is page 7. And we've already talked about 6 briefly, so let's now go to 7. And we see circles, and now we see rectangles, as -- no, that's not the right page. Sorry. Sorry, we need page 7, not map 7. There we go. And if you could just blow that a little more, we'll be able to see the -- So when you were talking about rectangles, is this what you meant?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just looking at the legend, is that correct, the rectangles are to represent schools and the circles are written in to represent mass executions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And is there any particular reason why this map is the only map that has rectangles on it of mass executions, when there was certainly mass executions alleged in the other parts of the map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I would not know that. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right, let's go to page 8, e-court page 10. Now, this looks like something new. What is this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This is again a simplified map, but this one was created by the OTP GIS unit using the same GIS data from Zagreb. And you can see the area stretching south from Rogatica to the north up to Batkovic, so just to show the general area of this eastern part of Bosnia. And then you can see the enclave boundaries or lines, which were taken from the Drina Corps map with ERN 0438-8412 and geo-referenced into this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next page, e-court 11. Now, if we could blow this up a little bit so we can read the writing in one of those boxes. Actually, let's look at the top box, because that will include Srebrenica. So what we can see here is a Cyrillic map with English in white underneath it. Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the map which was obtained -- or obtained again from Drina Corps collection, and it has the original ERN 0438-8415. What we have in front of us is already the scanned map of this original map, with the inserted translations. So this one was created for Popovic trial, so it is actually the scan of this same map with inserted translations of the text on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next page, then, 12 on e-court. Now, again we see a map. Can you just tell us, first of all, the background map with the basic map detail, without any of the colours, what is that, and what was on it originally when we obtained it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. This map we can see in front of us now, we compiled with three different maps, so we have used, as a base, three different maps from Drina Corps collection again. So they are ERN 0438-8412, the second one 0444-2916, and the last one, 0444-3118, because one of such maps did not include the entire area we wanted to include, so from Zepa up to Han Pijesak on the left-hand side, so -- and then we inserted these significant VRS positions and highlighted some roads into that map. So we created this map based on the ones I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What, if you can tell me, were you referring to just then when you said "we put the information on the map"? Was that the purple circles and the white boxes?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The circles, white boxes, and we highlighted some town names as Rogatica and Han Pijesak, and then you can see in purple some -- in purple you can see roads leading up -- up from Borike up to Han Pijesak, so that's what we have made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What, if you can recall, was on the original VRS map that we obtained from the Drina Corps collection, if anything?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. We can see, in the middle on the right-hand side, we can see the cross with four Cs, and then around -- and some yellow arrows and red arrows and this what is on the original map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this cross with the four Cs, are those actually four Cs?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. These are Cyrillic four Cs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are they Cs or some other letter in Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, these are S, Ss, four Ss. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know what that stands for? If you don't, I --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, all right. And again, Your Honours, we do have the original VRS maps for you to see what the original VRS information was and what we've put on it. All right, let's go to the next one, page 13 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this a different map from what we've seen before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This is a blow-up of the same map we discussed earlier, the map with translations. So this is a blow-up of the Zepa part of this same map with ERN 0438-8415. And, again, some original markings which were already there. You can see in blue the area of enclave and some red lines, so that was already there. So what we have put are those white boxes and circles around certain places. These are all our markings, and of course the legend on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next map, 14. Okay. There we see two of the Ss in Cyrillic on this map. Is that the same as the Cyrillic Ss that we saw -- the same map, just a different portion of it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. This is again compilation of those three maps I've told you before, so a compilation of the same maps. So it's just a blow-up, I would say, of the same area with some significant points -- VRS points at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is this purple highlighting that we see? Was that added by you or is that part of the original map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No, that was added by us. These purple lines are the roads leading up and down or around this area we can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next one, 15. What is this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This is the satellite image of the same area we have just viewed, so it's the area of Zepa or stretching south from Borike up to Han Pijesak. And this image was obtained from the -- I have to consult my report. It was obtained by the Supreme Headquarters, Allied Powers, Europe, in September of 2006. So when this image was taken, we don't know, but it's the image obtained from that source. So, and again, you can see some markings on this map, and these were inserted by us. So the image -- the original image was without any markings, it was a typical aerial image, and then all the markings you can see on this image were inserted by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, again, this purple highlighting, what is that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It's the same as the map before. These are roads -- different roads which are leading across the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just for basic knowledge, the red that we see on this and the blue, what do those indicate?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yeah, the red is the area of the enclave. Now, I'm -- no, sorry, it's -- yeah, it is taken from the map with four Ss, so the same red line. It has the same meaning here. It says, yeah, approximate location of the Serb positions at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the VRS maps that were obtained from the Drina Corps collection or from the Zvornik Brigade, did they traditionally mark the Serb positions in one colour and the Muslim positions in another?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The Serb positions are usually in red, and the Muslim positions are in blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right, let's go to the next page, 16. Now, this looks like a different map. What kind of map is this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yeah, so far we have been reviewing 1:50.000 maps, and this is the map of 1:25.000. So it means you can see more details in this map. And this is the area of the Borike and Boksanica, so it's a blow-up of the map. And the basis for this map was the map we obtained from NATO, NATO C-3 Agency here in The Hague, I would say in September of 2004. So they have provided this 1:25.000 map to us. And, again, these circles and blue texts and texts you can see on the map, we have inserted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page, 17. What is this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This is the blow-up of the area around Rogatica, showing significant positions around that town, which will be discussed in this case. And this map is based on the VRS and the Drina Corps collection map 0444-3118, so it's 1:50.000 map, this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And it's just a blow-up of that, so it makes it look bigger, I take it.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it's a blow-up. And the markings, direct markings you can see on the map, were ours, while the circle around Rogatica with number 62 you can see, you will find it on the original map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. The next one, 18?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It is again the area of Rogatica, but this is now 1:25.000 map again obtained from the same sources, C-3 NATO Agency, so it's again, you know, significant positions in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then 19. We can see it says "Approximate driving distance and driving time," and then from various places; Rogatica, Borike. And it gives the kilometres and the average time. Where did this information come from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Most of this information came from our missions. We were there on a mission, and we have been measuring these distances and driving times for most of them. For some of them, where we did not measure the actual times and distances, we have obtained these distances from the sources, from the -- yeah, from the sources, and then we have estimated the driving times. So I have participated in some of those missions, but for all of them, it was also my colleague, Erin Gallagher, who was present at most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what year or years was this done, were these roads driven and these miles noted -- kilometres noted?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yeah, this was done this year and last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so this would not include wartime conditions, roads in the war, or check-points, that sort of thing; this is just meant to be what you found recently?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And I assume the conditions are much different now, because there are asphalt roads now, and you can see there are new roads, and I don't know how it was at that time. Probably, they were not asphalt roads at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, I see we're just beyond our time. I will bring the original maps for the continuing of this, and then it will be over, and over to the general for cross-examination. And, of course, if we could speak to Mr. Janc about other things than this testimony, we would appreciate it for the next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Still one question from my colleague, Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes, again for the witness. The page I'm looking at of your book is 9. You can bring it up maybe on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's the map number 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes. At the top of the map, in white, there is an inscription, and I read: "Disposition of our enemy and UNPROFOR forces around the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa." Who is the owner of this map, who reproduced this map, and to what do those words refer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The owner of this map is the VRS. I would say for this particular map, it's Drina Corps. Drina Corps, yes. So they have wrote all these text on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This ends the examination-in-chief for today. You may return to your normal work. Thank you very much that you could make it to come here at short notice, but take -- bear in mind, please, that you should now, during the quite long break until the continuation of your testimony, that you shouldn't talk, about -- to either party about the content of your testimony. Of course, you are -- as a member of the OTP, entitled to talk to colleagues about your normal work. Thank you very much. We have to adjourn now, but I would like to know, next week, on the 22nd and 23rd, we are continuing the cross-examination of the Witness Ruez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And if we could, it would be good to just start with him and catch Mr. Janc when we can, because we really don't want to risk having to bring back Mr. Ruez again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think this is a very good idea. We should proceed in that way. I would like to mention a very short issue. Perhaps you'll remember, on the 25th of March, 2010, during the testimony of the Witness Oric, we had marked one document. It was a newspaper article only in English, tendered by the Defence. We were told by the CLSS that these articles will not be translated into B/C/S, so that it will be now an exhibit as tendered by the Defence. That means that the Defence Exhibit 18. We have to adjourn now and resume on the 22nd of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of April, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.52 p.m.,
